events.title: v1.0.0 A loopback Responses adapter
events.detail: The first release: a portable loopback Responses compatibility adapter with a watchdog, platform service adapters, bounded upstream retries and SSE reconnect handling.

events.title: v1.0.12 A retryable 503 after bounded recovery
events.detail: Once the pair-safe fallbacks are rejected, one final request carries only the latest instruction and the latest user request. Exhausted recovery and an exhausted DMXAPI 477 retry return a retryable 503 with Retry-After.

events.title: v1.0.43 One provider-portable grammar
events.detail: Every Responses replay request is projected onto a provider-portable grammar without changing Codex conversation storage. DMXAPI, UCloud/Azure and AIHubMix get fixed, isolated loopback routes.

events.title: v2.0.2 Codex Responses Proxy and a provider manifest
events.detail: Renamed from the DMX-specific Codex DMX Proxy, it serves ordinary Responses endpoints through a provider manifest. Every request names an explicit /<provider>/v1 namespace, and installation no longer reads or rewrites Codex or AIGW configuration.

events.title: v3.1.16 Upgrades keep admitting requests
events.detail: A capability-qualified upgrade or rollback handoff no longer rejects new and in-flight Responses requests with proxy_draining. Bounded draining remains only for replacing a legacy native generation.

events.title: v4.0.0 Upgrades need generations
events.detail: In-place upgrades require a durable generation-based installation; an older flat one must be uninstalled before a fresh install. Linux requires a reachable user service manager and keeps the host's lingering policy.

events.title: v5.0.0 OpenAI Responses Proxy
events.detail: The product, command, native service and release assets take the new name; existing installations migrate by uninstall and fresh installation. --upstream-base-url selects one ordinary Responses upstream at installation.

events.title: v5.0.3 The macOS watchdog returns after a restart
events.detail: With a GUI login, installation registers the watchdog in that login's domain, which launchd reloads at every GUI login. Background-only registrations from 5.0.1 and 5.0.2 are migrated.

events.title: v5.1.0 Body admission and one exchange deadline
events.detail: A Responses body needs one ASCII Content-Length, at most 64 MiB, received within 30 s; transfer encodings and missing or repeated lengths get 400. The upstream timeout becomes one deadline per exchange.

events.title: v5.1.3 Upstream redirects are not followed
events.detail: A redirect could carry the client's Authorization header to another host; the client now receives the redirect itself. Drain and handoff controls accept only a loopback caller that sends no Origin.

events.title: v5.1.7 A completely sent request is never resent
events.detail: 5.1.6 retried every transport failure, which can duplicate provider work and billing. The client now receives 502 upstream_outcome_unknown; failures before the request is complete are still retried.

events.title: v5.1.10 Input too long, media over budget
events.detail: An upstream input-length or media-budget rejection gets one attempt with less history when the current input permits. Current user and tool images, instructions and tool dependencies are kept.

events.title: v5.1.11 Option values outside their grammar are refused
events.detail: --port takes only a whole number written in decimal digits; 8.5 and 0x50 had run the command on ports 8 and 80. --timeout-seconds takes at most 3600, where inf had been a deadline without an upper bound. Each refused value is a usage error.

events.title: v5.1.12 A stream's error event ends the response
events.detail: A stream that the upstream ends with a top-level error event had reached the client as a broken connection. The client now receives the event and the end of the response, status --json reports the failure class stream_error, and the log names the event's code.

events.title: v6.0.0 A listener is replaced only by handoff
events.detail: The drain control is removed: its two routes, the 503 proxy_draining response and its counters, failure classes and health fields. Upgrade, rollback and reload replace a running listener only by handoff, and one that lacks a handoff capability is refused before any change. An installation written by 5.0.6 or earlier is refused instead of read with defaults.

events.title: v6.0.1 The log names how each admitted response ended
events.detail: The log names how every admitted response ended, and a client's close during a write is named once and ends the connection. A timed-out write of an upstream error or a local failure had drawn a second answer, 504 upstream_deadline_exceeded, which status reported as the last failure. Nothing more is written now. A stream whose handler met a failure it does not name left its connection open with an unfinished response body; the proxy now ends that connection.

events.title: v6.0.2 An unanswered handoff request is waited out
events.detail: A handoff request that ended without the listener's answer had been rolled back at once, while the listener could still begin the handoff. An upgrade or a rollback now waits for the request's timeout and one second, 31 seconds by default, and restores only if no handoff has begun. A listener refuses a request that it would begin after that timeout, with HTTP 408. recover waits 121 seconds before it restores an interrupted upgrade or rollback whose previous release still serves.

events.title: v6.0.3 An installation is read only through its selected generation
events.detail: An installed payload is read only through the generation the selector names, and payload files at the data root's own level are not the product's. Without a selected generation, status reports that no payload generation is selected, where it had reported an unavailable manifest. uninstall reads the payload generations before it removes the native service, so an invalid generations/ directory is refused before anything is removed. uninstall --purge of a data root without a generation that the product owns fails and preserves its content.

events.title: v7.0.0 Windows is no longer supported, and Suhe.AI gets a route
events.detail: Windows is no longer supported: a release publishes the macos-arm64 and linux-x86_64 assets only, and 6.0.3 is the last release with a Windows asset. An installation on macOS or Linux, and an upgrade there, are unchanged. A route for Suhe.AI sends Responses and model-catalog requests to suheai.cn through the same provider-portable projection as the other routes, with no provider-specific wire policy.

events.title: v7.0.1 DMXAPI receives a stateless first attempt as written
events.detail: The DMXAPI route sends the first attempt of a stateless request, with store=false and no previous_response_id, conversation or item reference, as the client wrote it. The release gave as its reason that DMXAPI answers a changed request without reasoning and without an error, so Codex conversations held on DMXAPI did not reason through the proxy. The portable grammar still admits or rejects every request, and every later attempt sends the projected request. The other routes are unchanged.

events.title: v7.0.2 DMXAPI again receives every attempt projected
events.detail: The DMXAPI route no longer sends the first attempt of a stateless request as the client wrote it. As before 7.0.1, every route builds every attempt from the projected request, and status --json no longer reports pass_through_projected_resends. 7.0.1 brought no measured benefit: an alternating measurement on the day of its release gave no reasoning from DMXAPI on any path, its own endpoint without the proxy included.

events.title: v8.0.0 The request path names the upstream
events.detail: A client's base URL names its upstream after the listener address, so a new upstream needs no release; the provider routes and install --upstream-base-url are gone. Data requests are served only to a loopback client that sends no Origin and no Fetch Metadata. The payload holds no providers.toml, so an installation of 7.0.2 or earlier is refused. The DMXAPI 477 retry and plaintext agent delivery are removed.
